messages.content: Ravi confirmed the Friday-to-Tuesday DC dates. Can you do one last pass and tell me exactly what to book tonight? I do not want to chase a tiny savings if it makes the airport or hotel awkward.

Yes. If these live prices are still showing, I would book the convenient DCA version. Pair A: Delta Main Cabin ATL-DCA Fri Apr 4 around 6:18 p.m.-7:59 p.m.; return Tue Apr 8 around 2:10 p.m.-3:58 p.m.; current total for three is roughly $1,110-$1,140. Hotel: Hampton Inn Washington-Downtown-Convention Center, two queens, cancellable, breakfast listed, 4+ guest rating, about $290-$305 before taxes. Pair B saves about $230 by flying into IAD, but adds a longer arrival transfer after a school-day departure. Pair C uses Residence Inn near the Convention Center: more space, usually $35-$45 more per night unless you take a prepaid rate.
Do we lose anything important with Hampton versus Residence Inn?

Mostly space. Hampton gives you two queen beds, breakfast, a simple Metro-friendly location, and a lower cancellable rate. Residence Inn is better if you want a studio layout, kitchenette, and a little more breathing room for three people. If the Residence Inn cancellable rate is only about $25-$30 more per night, I would consider it. If the only close price is prepaid, I would stay with Hampton.
Dulles savings look like about $240 total. Is that enough to switch?

I would not switch for $240 on this itinerary. After you account for either a longer Metro ride or rideshare from IAD, the real savings may be closer to $100-$150, and the arrival night becomes more tiring. I would only reconsider IAD if the DCA total jumps over about $1,250 or if the DCA seat map makes it impossible to keep Leela with one of you.
For the flight, Main Cabin not Basic, right?

Right. Book Main Cabin so you can choose seats and avoid the Basic Economy restrictions. Pick a three-seat row if available, ideally with one window. If the perfect row costs extra, I would pay a modest seat fee to keep Leela next to an adult, but not overpay for premium seats.
The Hampton rate I see says free breakfast and cancellation until April 2, then one-night penalty. That sounds okay?

That is workable. Before paying, confirm the room type is two queens, not one king, and check the final total after taxes. I would save a screenshot of the breakfast line and cancellation terms. Since you will not have a car, ignore parking costs unless they sneak in as a mandatory fee, which they should not.
I also see a prepaid Residence Inn rate that is only $15 more per night than Hampton. Tempting?

I would skip the prepaid rate for this trip. The dates are close, but family schedules and school-week travel still leave enough uncertainty that cancellable is worth more than the extra room. If a cancellable Residence Inn rate drops close to Hampton, then switch; otherwise Hampton is the cleaner choice.
Good. Give me the order with stop points.

Book in this order: 1. Buy Delta Main Cabin ATL-DCA Apr 4 and DCA-ATL Apr 8 if the total for three is at or below about $1,150. Stop and recheck if it is over $1,200 or only Basic Economy is available. 2. Select seats together during purchase, with a window in the row if available. 3. Book Hampton Inn Washington-Downtown-Convention Center only if it is two queens, cancellable until Apr 2, and breakfast is clearly included. Stop if the room changes to king-only, breakfast disappears, or the total jumps materially. 4. Save both confirmations, add the flights to the Delta app, and plan to check the seat map again at check-in.

memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Maya assessed a roughly 30-minute earlier DC outbound. Because the family had no checked bags, could leave school promptly, and still had seats together, she kept the DCA nonstop and confirmed hotel bag storage and breakfast timing.

messages.content: Delta just emailed a schedule change. Friday’s DCA flight is now 5:48 instead of around 6:20. We are two days out. Is that still realistic after school pickup?

It is tighter, but still realistic if you have no checked bags and can leave school promptly. For a 5:48 departure, boarding will likely start around 5:10. I would want you at ATL by about 4:15. The later nonstop option into IAD avoids the rush but gets you into the DC area later and adds a longer transfer, so I would not switch unless pickup is likely to slip.
No checked bags. Ravi can pick Leela up at 2:45, and I can be ready by 2:30. We will go straight from Decatur.

Then I would keep the DCA flight. If you are rolling from school by 3:05, you have a decent cushion even with traffic. Keep dinner expectations low at the airport, use mobile boarding passes, and go straight to security. The key is not adding a stop at home.
Can you check the Hampton details too? We may need them to hold bags Tuesday, and Saturday has an early museum start.

The Hampton Downtown-Convention Center details show luggage storage/front-desk bag hold for same-day guests, so Tuesday after checkout should be fine. Breakfast is listed as complimentary, with hours shown as 6:00-10:00 a.m.; that should work for an early museum morning. I would still ask at check-in in case weekend hours vary.
What about seats? I cannot tell if the time change moved anything.

The seat assignments still look together: one row outbound with a window and the return row together as well. Recheck when check-in opens, because equipment swaps can move seats, but I do not see a reason to change flights for seating right now.
Okay, let’s keep DCA. Anything else I should do today?

Keep the revised flight, do not move to IAD. Today: acknowledge the Delta schedule change, confirm the seats in the app, screenshot the hotel bag-hold and breakfast details, and set a Friday reminder to leave school by 3:05. No hotel change is needed.

messages.content: New one: I have a Cary client rollout May 6 through 9. Meetings start Tuesday, so I probably need to fly to RDU Monday evening. Can you rough out flights and hotel areas before I ask for approval?

Sure. I can frame it, but I would not lock the hotel until the exact office address is confirmed. For now I am assuming solo travel, ATL-RDU, hotel Monday May 5 through Friday May 9, and no rental car unless the address makes rideshare awkward. Is that right?
Yes. Solo, and I would rather avoid renting a car. The client has only said near Cary. Friday wrap-up might end before noon, but they have not promised.

Flight-wise, keep it simple with ATL-RDU nonstops. Monday evening, a departure around 6:00 p.m. arriving around 7:30 p.m. is the best balance because you can review materials and still get dinner. A later 8:00-ish departure works but makes the first morning feel rough. For Friday, hold two return options: around 2:20 p.m. if the wrap-up ends by noon, or around 4:55 p.m. if it may run long. I would avoid a CLT connection unless the nonstop price is unusually high.
Would a Tuesday morning flight be a terrible idea if the first meeting starts at 10?

Not terrible, but thin. An early ATL-RDU nonstop could land around 8:20, then you still need deplaning, rideshare, and traffic. For a 10:00 client start, any delay puts you in scramble mode. If the meeting starts at noon, Tuesday morning becomes reasonable. For a 10:00 start, Monday evening is safer.
Hotel should be easy after long days. Breakfast is helpful, but dinner nearby matters more than being downtown Raleigh.

Then I would focus on Cary or Cary-adjacent areas, not downtown Raleigh. Shortlist: Homewood Suites Raleigh-Cary/I-40 area, usually strong guest ratings, breakfast included, suites, and restaurants a short ride away; Courtyard Raleigh Cary/Crossroads or Parkside area, strong ratings and better dinner access, but breakfast may not be included; Hyatt Place Raleigh/Cary, decent practical option but better only if the office is east of Cary or closer to the arena/airport side.
Can you put those in order?

Provisional order: 1. Homewood Suites in the Cary/I-40 or Crossroads area if the office is central or west Cary, because breakfast and room setup are easy for four nights. 2. Courtyard Cary/Crossroads or Parkside if dinner access is the bigger priority and the rate is good, with breakfast treated as an extra cost. 3. Hyatt Place Raleigh/Cary only if the address points east or the price is clearly better. I would not book downtown Raleigh unless the client address changes.
What should I ask the client before we book?

Ask for the exact office address, Tuesday start time, Friday expected wrap-up time, the best rideshare drop-off entrance, and whether they have a preferred hotel or corporate rate. The office address is the biggest missing piece because near Cary can mean very different drive times.
Give me a provisional itinerary and not-to-exceed numbers for approval.

Provisional approval request: fly ATL-RDU Monday May 5 on a nonstop around 6:00 p.m., arriving around 7:30 p.m.; return RDU-ATL Friday May 9, either around 2:20 p.m. if the wrap-up is confirmed before noon or around 4:55 p.m. if not. Flight cap: $375 Main Cabin round trip. Hotel: cancellable 4+ guest-rated property in Cary/Crossroads/Weston Parkway area, ideally Homewood Suites or similar, May 5-9, breakfast included if available and dinner access nearby. Hotel cap: $210-$240 per night before taxes. Confirm the client address and Friday end time before purchase; choose a window seat if available after ticketing.
